interest: Consular celebrations in Japan and Taiwan, 1931–38.
overview: State Department Decimal File 894.463 (Entertainment in Japan by Resident Officers of the United States) covers the period from July 1931 to July 1938 and documents official social functions, national holiday commemorations, and hospitality provided by American consular officials stationed in Japan and Japanese-ruled Taiwan. The file comprises consular despatches, cross-reference sheets, speeches, liturgical programs, newspaper translations, and internal State Department memoranda originating from posts in Taihoku (Taipei), Nagoya, Kobe, Osaka, and Nagasaki. The records detail annual Fourth of July official receptions, the nationwide February 1932 George Washington Bicentennial celebrations, transit hospitality for Vice President John Nance Garner and a Congressional delegation visiting Kobe in 1935, and an informal flag-raising ceremony in Nagasaki in 1938, illustrating diplomatic protocol, consular interactions with Japanese civil and military elites, and the shifting tenor of bilateral relations in the 1930s.

subfiles.from: John B. Ketcham, American Consul, Taihoku
subfiles.summary: Consul Ketcham reports on the Fourth of July reception at the Taiwan Railway Hotel in Taihoku, attended by Taiwan Government General, military, naval, consular, and business figures; speeches, a toast to the President, favorable press coverage, and the Japanese flag flown over the Government General building.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 30 from Ketcham (Taihoku) on Independence Day Reception

subfiles.about: Text of Consul John B. Ketcham's address delivered at the official Independence Day reception in Taihoku on July 4, 1932.
subfiles.from: John B. Ketcham, American Consul, Taihoku
subfiles.summary: Enclosure copy of Consul Ketcham's July 4, 1932 address at the Taiwan Railway Hotel, marking the 157th anniversary of independence, calling for international cooperation amid economic hardship, recalling Perry's 1853 expedition, and voicing confidence in growing U.S.-Japan friendship and trade.
subfiles.title: Speech Delivered by Consul Ketcham at Independence Day Reception in Taihoku
subfiles.to: Guests at Independence Day Reception / Department of State

subfiles.about: Consular despatch reporting on the transit visit to Kobe of the Vice President, Speaker of the House, and Congressional party en route to the Philippines.
subfiles.from: Kenneth C. Krentz, American Consul, Kobe
subfiles.summary: Consul Krentz reports on the October 30, 1935 Kobe stopover of the S.S. President Grant carrying Vice President Garner, Speaker Byrns, and a Congressional party; staff arranged tours and a reception and dance for about one hundred Americans at the Oriental Hotel, with no incidents.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 546 from Krentz (Kobe) on Visit of Vice President and Congressional Party

subfiles.about: Consular despatch reporting on the official Fourth of July reception commemorating the 161st anniversary of American independence at the Osaka Consulate.
subfiles.from: C. R. Cameron, American Consul General, Osaka
subfiles.summary: Consul General Cameron reports on the 161st Independence Day reception at the Osaka Consulate, attended by about ninety guests including the Governor of Osaka, the Mayor, a Major General, a naval Admiral, consular colleagues, and resident Americans and Britons; the event received wide Japanese and English press coverage.
subfiles.title: Despatch from Cameron (Osaka) on Independence Day Reception

subfiles.about: Consular report on Fourth of July observances in Nagasaki, describing an informal morning flag-raising ceremony and the omission of a formal reception.
subfiles.from: Ralph Cory, American Vice Consul, Nagasaki
subfiles.summary: Vice Consul Cory reports on the July 4, 1938 Nagasaki Consulate celebration: a flag-raising ceremony and anthem followed by a buffet for Americans and Japanese officials, with no formal reception per Embassy policy, though the American Association held an evening picnic.
subfiles.title: Despatch from Cory (Nagasaki) on July Fourth Celebration and Flag-Raising

subfiles.about: Text of remarks delivered by Vice Consul Ralph Cory at the Independence Day flag-raising ceremony at the Nagasaki Consulate on July 4, 1938.
subfiles.from: Ralph Cory, American Vice Consul, Nagasaki
subfiles.summary: Enclosure containing Vice Consul Cory's July 4, 1938 address at the Nagasaki flag-raising, marking the 162nd anniversary of independence, thanking Japanese guests for friendship and hospitality, reflecting on the Declaration of Independence, and appealing to democratic and Lincolnian ideals for lasting peace.
subfiles.title: Remarks of Vice Consul Cory at Independence Day Flag-Raising Ceremony in Nagasaki
